name: Mental health therapist

pf.license.need: always: each therapist holds their own active license from the state's board for their kind of license (like a counselor, a social worker, a marriage and family therapist or a psychologist); the state's form says which licenses may give therapy
pf.license.who: each person; the practice too, where the state's form registers therapy practices (a switch)
pf.license.ask: each person's license type and number in their invite reply (or the owner sends it); an associate's supervisor; the practice's registration number, where the state's form asks for one
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.remote: a video session only with a therapist licensed in the state the client is in during that session, or holding a compact privilege or a temporary permit where the state's form allows it (a switch); the state is asked at booking and confirmed at the start of each video session
pf.license.associates: an associate (a therapist not yet fully licensed) sees clients only under the supervisor the state's form sets, and is booked directly only where the state's form allows it (a switch)
pf.license.familyTherapy: family therapy as its own kind of work needs a family therapist's license where the state's form licenses it on its own; other licensed therapists may offer it where their license covers it (a switch)
pf.license.agreement: a health privacy agreement (a HIPAA business associate agreement) signed on the secure page before the first booking
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form or a plan asks for it
pf.license.substanceUse: a substance-use program that federal confidentiality rules cover isn't booked through Rosie at launch: the request gets the office's own line, and nothing is kept (Rosie's decision until a service agreement exists)

pf.services.shape: one client with one therapist at a time, each session a set length; a new client starts with a free fit check call, then a longer first session; ongoing sessions are weekly, with a weekly time the client says yes to; in a couples or family session, each adult confirms on their own page
pf.services.examples: the example practices' own prices (Lee Associates at the office and by video, Lee Family Services at clients' homes), not a standard; with a health plan, the client pays the plan's copay and the plan pays the rest

pf.services.notOffered: medicine (no prescribers at the example practices); substance-use treatment under federal confidentiality rules (handed to the office's own line); psychological testing (only where a psychologist offers it, after a consult)
pf.services.capacity: one client, couple or family per therapist at a time; the office's one larger room for couples sessions
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: the client is always there
pf.services.online: video sessions count as at the office: every session but a couples session at the example office, and only with a therapist licensed for where the client is that day

pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a teen alone only where the state's form lets a teen consent and the practice turns it on (a switch); a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; someone else may pay, but the client agrees for themselves
pf.questions.neverAsked: the reason for therapy, symptoms, diagnoses, medicine names and a child's details are never asked in the AI chat or by text: only on the secure page

stop.say: If you're thinking about harming yourself, call or text 988 now. If you're in danger right now, call 911.
stop.booking: 988 and 911 first, at once, every time; danger right now, unsure, or no answer: no booking in that chat; only a person who clearly says they're safe now and still wants to book may go on: the AI says a first session may be days away and 988 is there any time, and a clinician is told the same day; a booking never stands in for 988 or 911

stop.words: harming someone else, or anyone in danger right now
stop.say: If anyone is in danger, get to safety and call 911 now. You can also call or text 988.
stop.booking: no booking; if the person is already a client, the owner is alerted at once, any hour, under the office's crisis rule

goOn.words: not feeling safe at home (someone there hurts or threatens them)
goOn.what: 911 if anyone is in danger now; then the booking goes on, reaching the person only the safe way they pick

goOn.words: stress, worry, poor sleep or feeling low, with nothing above
goOn.what: no safety message; matched to a first session; Rosie never judges how serious anything is

pf.safety.always: the general screen on every message, call and intake answer: danger to life, a medical emergency or self-harm gets 911 or 988; Rosie never counsels or gives advice, only booking
pf.safety.crisisRule: the office's own crisis rule, set by the owner at sign-up (a switch): who is alerted at once, any hour (the owner, or the client's therapist), and who gets it if it isn't opened in 15 minutes; the alert has a link, never the words
pf.safety.forms: a yes about self-harm on an intake form reaches a clinician the same day, never waiting for the session

steps.name: Fit check call
steps.when: before the first session, at least a day before; booked with it on one secure link
steps.result: a good fit: the first session stands; another therapist fits better: the client OKs the change; not a fit: cancelled with nothing charged, and a clinician calls with other options

steps.name: Intake forms and consent
steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; due the day before; one reminder
steps.who: every client, and each adult in a couples or family session
steps.result: not done: the owner keeps the session (signed on the secure page before it starts), moves it, or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the desk, by hand
steps.who: every client who names a plan
steps.result: covered (the copay shows), some services only, not covered (self-pay, or a free cancel), or can't check now (the desk checks by the next business day)

steps.name: A written good-faith estimate
steps.when: told while booking; sent on time, as the federal rules say
steps.result: a to-do for the desk, with its due date; Rosie delivers it and records when

steps.name: The plan's OK for sessions ahead
steps.when: where a plan asks for it, by the desk on the plan's own website
steps.result: the desk records the sessions approved and the end date; Rosie warns before they run out

steps.name: Past records
steps.when: only with the client's signed OK
steps.who: where the therapist asks for them
steps.result: office to office, never through Rosie; a session isn't held up for them

pf.first_steps.prep: for a video session, a quiet, private place and a charged phone; for a home session, a room with a door; the intake forms done the day before

pf.visit.checkIn: at the office: the code at the front desk, or to the therapist when nobody is at the desk; by video: read out at the start; at home: the code at the door
pf.visit.beforeWork: the therapist reads the intake forms; at a video session, the therapist confirms the client's name and where they are, for the license and in case of an emergency (Rosie's rule everywhere, and the state's form where it requires it)
pf.visit.changes: nothing is added during a session; a longer session is booked ahead; the next step, like a weekly time, is agreed in the room and confirmed by the client's own yes by text
pf.visit.done: the code or DONE; session notes stay in the practice's own record, never in Rosie or a text; Rosie keeps only booking notes
pf.visit.missed: the therapist calls first after a missed session, before any fee; at home, a client who doesn't answer starts a safety check: the client, the emergency contact, then the office's crisis rule
pf.visit.home: at home, the therapist checks the room is private, and leaves at once if they feel unsafe (they text UNSAFE)

pf.money.before: a card saved at booking, nothing taken: it pays the copay or the self-pay fee after the session, and the late-cancel fee only if the owner confirms; a fee-free client saves no card
pf.money.plans: the plans the practice takes (its own list); the desk checks each plan by hand and records it: active or not, in network, the copay, any deductible left, and whether the plan must OK sessions ahead; the copay is an estimate, not a promise
pf.money.selfPay: a self-pay or uninsured client hears while booking that they can get a written good-faith estimate, and gets it on time; a bill far above it can be disputed (the federal rules set how)
pf.money.outOfNetwork: the client pays the self-pay fee, and the receipt on the secure page has what their plan needs to pay them back (a superbill)
pf.money.slidingScale: an owner's switch: a lower self-pay fee for a few spots, asked only on the secure page, each fee OK'd by the owner; never asked about by text or through the AI
pf.money.after: at the office: the copay or fee at the front desk when it's open, or the saved card at DONE when nobody is at the desk (Saturdays, evenings) and for video; at home: the saved card at DONE, or the office's own way when a plan pays; a balance after the plan pays is billed by the practice, never by Rosie's text
pf.money.fees: the late-cancel or missed-session fee: $75 at the example office (the old flowchart's own number), $89 at home, with less than 24 hours' notice; the same fee for every client who may be charged one; only when the owner confirms; never billed to a plan
pf.money.feeFree: a switch from the state's and the plan's rules: no fee ever for clients a plan or the rules protect (like Medicaid, where that applies); for some plans, like Medicare, only if every client pays the same fee; the owner can mark any client fee-free; their texts say 'No fee to cancel or miss'
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per booking applies to this work, as to every kind of work (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, shown at sign-up for the owner's yes; a booking the business puts in itself carries no $2; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee, paid to Stripe
pf.money.caps: fee limits for plan clients: from the plan's and the state's rules (switches)
pf.money.packages: none sold: each session is paid when it happens
pf.money.repeatPlans: a weekly time's sessions are each paid when they happen; no plan charge, and nothing paid ahead

pf.messages.displayName: a switch: the practice texts under a plain display name, like Lee Associates or Lee Family Services; card statements show it too
pf.messages.never: client texts carry only the display name, the date, the time, the place and a secure link: never 'therapy', 'counseling', the kind of session, a reason, a diagnosis, a medicine name or a child's details; at the office, never the therapist's name (it's on the secure page); at home, the therapist's name and photo stay, for the door check; the video link stays on the secure page
pf.messages.staff: texts to the owner and staff use the client's initials (A.M.), the time and a link: never health details, diagnoses, medicine names or a child's details; a client's question or crisis words go behind a link, never quoted
pf.messages.safeContact: the client says if texts and voicemail are safe; if not, Rosie reaches them only the way they pick
pf.messages.minors: a teen's texts go to the parent or guardian, unless the state's form lets the teen consent alone and the practice turns that on
pf.messages.noRatings: no rating or review request is ever sent to a client
pf.messages.noAdvice: Rosie gives no advice or counseling by text or chat; it answers only about booking

pf.staff.licenses: each therapist's own license, per state, and any compact privilege; an associate's supervisor on file
pf.staff.skills: who sees adults, teens, couples and families; who offers video and home sessions; who speaks which language; how each lists themselves (like a woman or a man) for clients who ask
pf.staff.supervision: an associate works only under the supervisor the state's form sets (a switch)
pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs same-day sessions, new clients where he turns that on, any custom price and every sliding-scale fee, and anything a therapist flags
pf.staff.standIn: a client's therapist is never changed without the client's own yes; a stand-in is offered only with the same skills and what the client asked for, like a woman
pf.staff.crisis: the owner, or the clinician the office's crisis rule names, gets crisis alerts at any hour
pf.staff.homeVisits: only therapists cleared for home sessions go to homes

pf.rules.records: therapy records are kept by the practice as long as the state's rules require (a child's may be longer); Rosie keeps only booking and payment records, and a delete removes only those
pf.rules.copies: a client's copy of their records within the time the rules set; Rosie sends only booking and payment records
pf.rules.minors: who may consent for a teen, at what age a teen may consent alone, and whether a parent is told (switches from the state's form)
pf.rules.telehealth: video sessions follow the state the client is in during the session; the state's form may require recording where the client is, a consent for video, or an emergency plan (switches)
pf.rules.goodFaith: the written good-faith estimate for self-pay and uninsured clients, on the federal timeline (a to-do with its due date)
pf.rules.substanceUse: substance-use programs under federal confidentiality rules aren't booked through Rosie at launch
pf.rules.showLicense: the license shown where the state asks: posted at the office, and on the listing
pf.rules.ads: no claims the state's rules don't allow
pf.rules.noRatings: no testimonials or ratings from clients (counseling and psychology ethics codes)
pf.rules.aiRules: where a state limits AI in mental health care, Rosie only books and never counsels; the state's form adds any notice it requires (a switch)
pf.rules.privacy: health privacy rules for every message and form; the business associate agreement before going live

pf.edges.crisis: crisis words in any message, at any time, get 988 and 911 first, and alert the owner under the office's rule; the booking stays
pf.edges.lateArrival: a late client is seen in the time left, and the session ends on time; no fee for running late
pf.edges.missedSession: the therapist calls first; at home, a client who doesn't answer starts a safety check before any fee
pf.edges.standIn: a therapist out: new times with the same therapist, or another only with the client's yes
pf.edges.forms: forms not done: one reminder, then the owner keeps the session (signed first), moves it, or cancels with no fee
pf.edges.planChange: the plan check comes back not covered: self-pay, or a free cancel
pf.edges.approvalRunsOut: the plan's approved sessions run low: the desk is warned, and asks for more or tells the client the self-pay price
pf.edges.outOfState: a video client who'll be in another state: only a therapist licensed there, another time, or a free cancel
pf.edges.twoBookings: a client with several sessions booked: Rosie asks which one before any change
pf.edges.healthQuestion: a question about what to do, or about medicine, goes to the therapist behind a link; Rosie gives no advice
pf.edges.weather: home sessions move with no fee when ice or snow warnings make the roads unsafe
pf.edges.unsafeHome: a therapist who feels unsafe at a home leaves (UNSAFE), and the owner calls
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way

From: physical-therapist (itself built from the dentist pilot, reviewed). Why: it runs the closest to therapy: sessions of a set length with a named clinician, forms only on the secure page, the plan checked by hand, no $2, a second side at the client's home, and a series of visits booked with the client's own yes. Its money paths are exactly this work's (A: list|card|card, list|card|counter, list|none|counter; B: list|card|card, list|none|own). Primary-care has video visits but no saved-card paths; chiropractor has set start times at home but no series.
Names: Sam Lee, a licensed therapist, owns Lee Family Counseling LLC (texts as 'Lee Family Services'; the master's main company: in-home therapy and family therapy, 410 Main St, a 25-mile area) and Lee Counseling Associates LLC (texts as 'Lee Associates'; the office at 40 Linden Ave, and video). The plain display names are the plug-in's switch; the legal names show only in sign-up (S1-09, S1-40).
People: Riley became Maya (office; couples, teens and home visits), Avery became Iris (office and video), Jordan became David (in-home sessions; his family therapist license is checked on its own), Casey became Elena (an associate therapist under Sam's supervision). Sam, Pat and Alex M. stay. Alex is never given a pronoun.
Kinds of work: plumbing became in-home therapy, electrical became family therapy (it waits for David's family therapist license, where the state's form licenses it on its own), the barbershop became the office practice. Every license rule is a switch from the state's form.
Prices are the example practices' own, not a standard: first session $190, weekly $160, couples $180, teen $160, 30 more minutes $80, a plan's $35 copay (the master's $35), late-cancel fee $75 at the office (the old flowchart's own number; the master's $20 read low for therapy) and $89 at home; in-home first session $179 (the master's), then $150; family session $199 ($249 when Sam leads it); the fit check call is free.
Money A: list|card|card is the main path (Saturday, nobody at the desk: the $35 copay goes on the saved card when Maya texts DONE). list|card|counter: the desk is open, the copay is paid there, and the card is only for the $75 fee. list|none|counter: a fee-free client (a plan that bars fees): nothing taken, no card. Left out: holds, deposits and full price (therapy is never paid ahead), photo or at-the-session pricing (every session is on the list), and Rosie's texted bill.
Money B: list|card|card is the main path (Alex pays out of pocket, out of network: $179 charged at DONE, a receipt for Alex's own plan). list|none|own: a plan pays in network and bars late fees, so nothing is taken and the office bills it its own way. Left out: holds, deposits, full price, a texted bill, photo or at-the-session pricing.
Sign-up words changed to how therapy is paid (S1-12 to S1-18, S1-41 to S1-47): in-home sessions save a card and charge it at DONE (Sam taps 2 at S1-15); family sessions a plan pays are billed the office's own way (S1-38); the office saves a card for the copay and the $75 fee, pays at the desk when it's open and by card at DONE on Saturdays, evenings and video.
Self-pay: the good-faith estimate notice before the yes, and the written estimate as a to-do with its federal due date (A4-41, A4-58, A7-30, B4-28, B7-30, S11-72).
